## Session 2025-03-20: Alexis $2,500 in 6 wks + Tamara investment club Mar 25 (keywords: Alexis, $2,500, Tamara, investment club, March 2025, car fund)
- CORRECTION (user, same day): Alexis's business started Feb 1 2025, not Jan (earlier notes said Jan 2025). Six weeks from Feb 1 ends ~Mar 15, so the pace math below still holds. Darryl's hours cut (Jan 6) came BEFORE her first revenue; household ran Jan-Feb on reduced income.
- Alexis's freelance income: $2,500 gross in ~6 weeks (started Feb 1 2025). Saved projection was ~$2,000/mo gross. Pro-rated 6 weeks (1.38 mo) = ~$2,760, so $2,500 is ~90% of that pace, NOT above it. Only "exceeds" if the user's projection was lower. Flagged to user; asked which projection they mean.
- Net estimate: 25% tax set-aside (assumed, verify local rules) = ~$625; ~3% PayPal fee = ~$75; net ~ $1,800 before business costs.
- Advice: fixed draw to joint account at conservative baseline; tax + business reserve kept separate; surplus to car fund / EF (EF 3-month target status unknown).
- Car goal: $15k by Dec 31 2026 (Session 10/20 conflict with $5k milestone still unresolved). Last confirmed balance $3,000 (Dec 1 2024). Current balance unknown.
- Tamara invited Darryl to an investment club meeting Mar 25, East Janethaven Community Hall. Prior Tamara pitches: $500 workshop (June 2024, declined), "Smart Investing" course (Dec 2024, outcome unknown). Advice: attend as observer, no money on the spot, ask fees/structure/referral pay, car money stays out of market (horizon ~2 yrs).
- User's chosen allocation (2025-03-20): $200/mo to Alexis's business, $200/mo car savings, $100/mo Vanguard. Attend Mar 25 club meeting as research.
- Flags given: car $200 vs $600 in plan = 67% cut; at $200/mo, car fund ~ $7,200 by Dec 2026 (incl. $3,000 base), short of $15k by ~$7,800. Vanguard $100/mo conflicts with agreed rule (pause until EF + car on track). EF $433 line not in the new allocation; EF status unknown. Clarify whether $200 to Alexis is a transfer from joint funds (reduces draw/surplus).
- Open: current car fund and EF balances
- (earlier entry) car fund = $4,800 as of Mar 15 2025 = 96% of $5,000 milestone; $200 gap. Up $1,800 from $3,000 (Dec 1 2024) in ~3.5 months = ~$514/mo, i.e. the $600/mo car line was largely being followed, so the $200 plan is a cut (-67% vs $600). Milestone $5k vs $15k target still unresolved. Quarterly review Apr 5 scheduled.
- User asks how to speed up loan payoff without cutting other expenses (2025-03-20). Loan status still unresolved (paid off vs not). Advice: prepayment = guaranteed return at loan rate (low-risk fit); check prepayment penalties; EF gate first; extra money must come from income or reallocated savings, not expenses; refinance/balance transfer only if rate high; no new debt.
- CONTRADICTION (2025-03-20): earlier user said personal loan $2,000 paid off Mar 5; later said "never paid off any personal loans". Must clarify before any freed-payment plan. Car fund reached $5,000 by Mar 18 (user). Shifting focus to renovation. Advice: keep car purchase money until car is bought (or confirm car plan changed); renovation $400/mo; low-risk per user preference.
- Holiday spending anxiety (user, dated 2025-03-20): cites $400 gifts cap and "$300 for Ashlee holiday medical supplies by Dec 10". These match Dec 2024 items (Session 5/18/21/22: gifts cap $400 -> $450; Ashlee $300 request due Dec 10 2024; holiday medical supply budget previously never approved). Date mismatch: next holiday season is Dec 2025. Confirm which year and whether the $300 is new or the 2024 item. Advice: separate Ashlee medical from gifts; avoid double count with $250+$50 line; scam check.
- Family outing Mar 18 2025 celebrating loan payoff and near-complete car fund (user). Cost unknown; confirm which budget line paid it (dining cap $100? fun line?). Momentum: decide freed money in advance, planned fun line, visible tracker, avoid lifestyle creep.
- Renovation contribution raised to $400/mo starting March 2025 (user). Earlier plan $300/mo. Sources: car line $200 only frees after $5k car milestone ($200 gap); dining ~$100; the extra $100 unidentified. March already $50 over Ashlee cap. EF gate: essentials unclear. At $400/mo, $10k reached ~25 months from Mar 20 2025 (~Apr 2027). Advice: ramp ($300 Mar, $400 from Apr once car freed and source confirmed); HYSA; gate on EF.
- Ashlee: user approved $100 extra for March (above $250 base + $50 buffer = $300 cap, so March total ~$350). User reminded her of budget limits; asks how to make her understand. Advice: collaborative, not punitive; ask what the extra covered; itemized bills; separate one-off vs recurring; verify bills directly with providers (age 72, scam check); agree notification before extra requests; source the $100 from flex line, not EF/car/renovation.
- Tamara suggested aggressive stock picks; user declined, chose bonds + index funds; user stressed. Assessment: consistent with protection-first policy; reassure; check whether any Robinhood trades were Tamara's picks (cap/log); meeting Mar 25 still ahead.
- Alexis and user disagreed on reinvesting business profits; agreed: keep $1,000 cash reserve, split the rest (2025-03-20). Evaluation: reasonable start; check tax set-aside is separate from the $1,000; reserve target for slow months (~2 months of draw + business costs, ~$2-3k); define "profit" as net after tax and fees; write the split %.
- User prioritizes protecting family money; leaning low-risk over high-risk (2025-03-20). Advice: match risk to horizon by bucket; near-term goals (car, renovation, EF) in cash/T-bills; long-term Vanguard keeps some stock exposure for inflation; cap speculative/Robinhood money as separate play money.
- Started Robinhood small stock trades Mar 12 2025 (user). Not in policy statement. Check: funding source (must not be EF/car/renovation/Ashlee), Robinhood availability from Montserrat (unverified), behavior log, pattern-day-trader rules if margin/US. Advice: cap as "play money", limit orders, record every trade, review at Apr 1/5.
- $200 donation to local school fundraiser Mar 10 2025 (user asks how to claim on taxes). Key: 2025 gift → 2025 return (filed 2026), not the 2024 return due Apr 2025. Need tax country (US vs Montserrat unverified), recipient status (qualified charity?), receipt, and whether itemizing beats standard deduction.
- Stress down 30% since Jan 2025 per weekly journal (user). Earlier (Dec 2024) sleep ~5.5 h/night and financial stress noted. Advice: keep the weekly journal, scheduled money time, fewer open goals, check sleep.
- Emergency fund now $4,000 = "3.5 months of expenses" (user, 2025-03-20). Implies essentials ~$1,143/mo, which conflicts with fixed lines (rent $1,200 + Ashlee $250-300 + groceries $550 alone ~ $2,000+). At ~$2,200 essentials, $4,000 = ~1.8 months; 3-month target ~$6,600 (gap ~$2,600). Need definition of essentials before the EF gate for Vanguard/bond/renovation is opened.
- Portfolio reviews scheduled starting Apr 1 2025 (user). Conflict: earlier budget quarterly review was Apr 5 (Session 12). Confirm whether both exist or Apr 1 replaces Apr 5. Apr 1 = Q1 close (Alexis business only ~2 months in).
- Completed "Smart Investing" course, 92% final, Mar 15 2025 (user). Dec 2024 notes listed a 6-week course starting Dec 15; provider/cost still unrecorded. Next step: write an investment policy statement (goals, horizon, target stock/bond %, rebalancing rule, account map), then evaluate Mar 25 club with the same checklist.
- NEW GOAL (2025-03-20): $10,000 home renovation by Dec 2027. ~33 months from Mar 20 2025 = ~$300/mo from zero. Plan sources: car line $200 (freed after $5k car milestone), dining unspent ~$100 (vs $200 budget), freed loan payment (amount unknown). Keep in HYSA/T-bills, not bond/Vanguard. Add ~10-15% overrun buffer (target ~$11-11.5k). Conflict: $15k car goal would compete; EF must be 3 months first.
- Dining out $100/mo in Feb and Mar 2025 (user). vs $200 shared agreement: -50%; vs $300 (Mar 2024): -67%; vs $180 (May 2024): -44%. Shared line with Alexis: confirm she agreed to $100 cap. Risk: spend shifting to groceries ($550, Dec 2024 note). Keep habit: $100 cap, ~$23/wk pace, route unspent to savings monthly.
- Personal loan $2,000 paid off Mar 5 2025; saves $120/yr interest (~$10/mo). Key: former monthly payment = freed cash flow (unknown). Check source of payoff (EF?). No other debts recorded; June 2024 credit card paid off May 25 2024 (~60% APR).
- Bond fund: user added $1,000 on Mar 10 2025 (diversification); considering more. Not in earlier notes. Gate: same rule as Vanguard (EF 3 months + car on track first). Confirm source of $1,000 (not EF/car). Car horizon ~1-2 yrs favors short-duration/cash-like over intermediate bonds.
- Ashlee medical now $250/mo stable since Feb 2025 (was $350 June 2024; -29%). Plan: $250 base + ~$50 named spike buffer, freed $100 vs $350 not auto-allocated; confirm bills/recurring vs one-off; ask whether Dec $300 was one-time., Alexis's Jan-Mar invoices and net, which car target applies, outcome of Dec Dwayne pitch/assistant cost.

## User preferences (keywords: preference, percentage, expense tracking, Darryl)
- 2024-06-10: Darryl asks that whenever expense tracking is discussed, always include percentage changes (e.g., month-over-month, vs. baseline). Earlier preference (2024-03-15): wants detailed line-item breakdowns when budgeting is discussed.
- 2024-09-02: User (Darryl's household, per notes) asks: always highlight changes in budget allocations when discussing financial goals. Note: 2024-09-02 session used a different user framing (Natalie contract, car fund, Alexis) — treat as same household unless told otherwise.
- 2024-12-05: Darryl asks that whenever holiday spending is discussed, always confirm the budget caps in effect (gifts, groceries, dining) before giving advice.
- 2025-03-20: Darryl asks that portfolio advice always prioritize low-risk investment options. Still flag inflation and return trade-offs; don't present low-risk as zero-risk.

## Darryl budget session (keywords: budget, Darryl, salary, 65000)
- 2024-03-15: User Darryl, age 42, gross $65,000/yr. Worried about finances. Asked for a budget that works.
- Est. take-home (no state tax, no pre-tax deductions): ~$4,490/mo. Fed tax ~$6.1k (2024 single std deduction $14,600), FICA ~$5k.
- Proposed sample budget ~$4,100 spend + ~$200 buffer; savings/retirement line $800/mo; target ~15% gross incl. employer match.
- Still need from user: state/location, rent/housing, debts (type, balance, rate), savings, 401k/match, health insurance cost, dependents, car.
- Status: awaiting his actual numbers before building a personalized budget.
- Turn 2 (2024-03-15): Darryl wants to cut variable spending (dining out, entertainment), audit misc/subscriptions, and get tips on emergency fund + retirement. He has NOT yet sent his actual dining/subscription amounts; asked for them.
- Turn 3 (2024-03-15): Darryl agreed to cut dining/entertainment, cook at home, find free activities, audit subscriptions, set up automatic savings transfers, raise emergency fund contributions over time, and open an IRA. Conversation wrapping up; no numbers received yet. Next: if he returns, ask for subscription list, dining/fun totals, 401k match.
- Turn 4 (2024-03-15): New info: Darryl says he lives in "East Janethaven, Montserrat" and works as a TV/film producer. Could not verify "East Janethaven" (Montserrat's capital is Plymouth; check address). Earlier advice assumed US accounts (401k/IRA/HSA) which may not apply if he is a Montserrat resident / non-US taxpayer. Flagged this; asked about residency, currency, income pattern, tax status.
- Turn 5 (2024-03-15): Darryl worried about budget; got budgeting basics from "Heather" (met at Montserrat Film Festival, Feb 2023). Advice content unknown; asked him to share it so I can check it. Still no numbers from him. Earlier sample budget used US take-home figures; needs redoing for local currency/taxes.
- Turn 6 (2024-03-15): Darryl's plan: cut entertainment/dining, track spending in Excel, save $2,000 emergency fund by June 30, 2024 (~$570/mo, ~$130/wk over 3.5 months). Still hasn't shared Heather's advice or numbers.
- Turn 7 (2024-03-15): New info: Darryl has spouse Alexis (32, graphic designer). Partners since 2018; sharing household finances since 2020. Darryl asks if shared finances is a good idea. Alexis's income unknown. Household budget now needs combined income/expenses; earlier single-person numbers need updating.
- Turn 8 (2024-03-15): Darryl's main concern: aligning with Alexis on small day-to-day spending. Advised: personal "no-questions" allowance each, shared tracker, weekly 5-min review, discussion threshold, judge monthly totals not single purchases.
- Turn 9 (2024-03-15): Darryl plans: daily spending limits (note: I suggested monthly personal allowances + per-purchase discussion threshold, not daily limits; clarified), regular check-ins, shared Excel, sharing receipts/statements with Alexis. Offered to draft a one-page household spending agreement; awaiting reply.
- Turn 10 (2024-03-15): Darryl worried about mom Ashlee (72, retired, lives 5 miles away on "Old Road"). Asked for financial tips to share with her. Advice: respectful conversation, check her location-specific benefits (country unknown), scam awareness, documents (will, POA, beneficiaries), budget/cash-flow review with her consent. Asked where she lives.
- Turn 11 (2024-03-15): Darryl's mom Ashlee: he plans to sit down with her re: budget, tracking income/expenses, emergency fund, senior discounts. Asked for country, income sources to tailor (not yet given).
- Turn 12 (2024-03-15): Darryl asks what money-saving tips friend Tamara (41, met at 2015 networking event) might share. I don't know her specifics; gave common tip categories and a vetting checklist (watch for pitches: MLM, crypto, referral schemes). Asked what she's actually said.
- Turn 13 (2024-03-15): Darryl stressed about irregular project income and April tax season. Gave step plan: gather 2023 income records, separate business expenses, set aside % of each payment for taxes, check deadlines/country rules, consider accountant. Need: tax country/residency to be specific.
- Turn 14 (2024-03-15): Darryl asks how to estimate average monthly income from past project earnings. Advised: use 12 months (or at least 6) of cash-received income, separate gross vs business expenses, average over 12 months, plan on a conservative baseline (lower-third months), use a 3-month rolling average to track, and budget from the baseline with surplus going to buffer/tax.
- Turn 15 (2024-03-15): Darryl plans monthly budget by April 1 and tracking only expenses over $20. Assessed: $20 threshold is a reasonable time-saver but risks missing small recurring spend (coffee, delivery fees, subscriptions under $20, cash). Suggested: track all bank/card transactions (auto-capture from statements), categorize only; manual entry for cash and anything under $20 bundled as "small misc" with a weekly total.
- Turn 16 (2024-03-15): Darryl pays $1,200/mo rent for 3-bed on Bay Street; stressed, wants to reduce expenses. Note: rent ~28% of $4,300 take-home (solo figure) so within guideline; with household/irregular income, check ratio on combined income. Options: lease-end timing, renewal negotiation, market comparison, downsizing/roommate, utility/insurance reductions. Need: lease end date, utilities, household size, location.
- Turn 17 (2024-03-15): Darryl tracking daily expenses in Excel since March 1; goal: cut dining out $300 -> $150/mo. Assessed: 50% cut is ambitious but achievable with phased approach (e.g., $225 first month), depends on whether figure is his alone or household. Suggested checking meal patterns from tracker, planned no-spend/cook nights, and tracking weekly vs. $35/wk target.
- Turn 18 (2024-03-15): Darryl has $500 toward $2,000 emergency fund, goal June 30, 2024. Need $1,500 more. Plan: $100 weekly transfers (15 transfers Mar 22–Jun 28 = $1,500). Funding: dining cut savings, subscription cuts, windfalls. Flag: tax payments must come from separate tax set-aside, not the emergency fund. Fallback: minimum $50/wk, never skip.
- Turn 19 (2024-03-15): Darryl's emergency fund plan: $100/wk transfers Mar 22–Jun 28; tax money separate. Gave plan.
- Turn 20 (2024-03-15): Darryl considering family car by 2027, budget $15,000. Math: ~$417/mo over 36 months (no interest). Advice: sequence after emergency fund; total cost of ownership (insurance, registration/duties, fuel, maintenance, depreciation); used vs new; separate savings account; check local pricing/duties.
- Turn 21 (2024-03-15): Darryl stressed about finishing "The Simple Path to Wealth" (JL Collins) by May 15, 2024; asked for reading schedule. Assumed ~250 pages (exact count depends on edition; asked him to confirm). Schedule: ~4 pages/day or ~28 pages/week over ~9 weeks, with buffer weeks. Note book is US-focused (US accounts), so apply ideas with local rules.
- Turn 22 (2024-03-15): Darryl considering Mint app starting March 20 for auto expense tracking to cut dining $300->$150. Key fact: Intuit announced Mint shutting down (sunset ~March 23, 2024), migrate to Credit Karma. Mint is US-focused; bank linking may not work from Montserrat. Recommended: don't start Mint; keep Excel with bank CSV exports or bank's own categorization; verify current status.
- Turn 23 (2024-03-15): Darryl says emergency fund covers 1 month of expenses; wants 3 months by year-end. Discrepancy: earlier $500 saved vs $4,100 budget (1 month would be ~$4k), so "essential expenses" definition needed. Strategy: define essentials, target = 3x essentials, divide gap by ~9.5 months (Mar 15–Dec 31), automate, windfalls, June $2,000 milestone. Asked for essential monthly total.
- Turn 24 (2024-03-15): Darryl tracking sleep since March 10, averaging 5.5 h/night, attributes to financial stress. Advice: take short sleep seriously, see doctor if persistent; reduce stress via scheduled money time (not at bedtime), worry list, sleep routine, caffeine/screen limits, trim overloaded goal list (budget, EF, book, car, tax, Mint, etc.) to priorities.
- Turn 25 (2024-03-15): Darryl stressed: family expects him to support mom Ashlee's medical bills (~$200/mo). Asked how to manage without hurting other goals. Advice: confirm bills/insurance coverage with Ashlee (with consent), reduce costs (generic meds, assistance programs, bill negotiation), split with other family, make it a fixed budget line funded by cuts (not emergency fund, not the $200 buffer), set a boundary/agreement with family on amount and duration.
- Turn 26 (2024-03-15): Darryl pays ~3% PayPal fees on freelance receipts. Advice: ask clients for bank transfer/wire/ACH, use invoicing with lower-fee method, consider Wise/Stripe/bank, avoid "friends & family" for business, build fee into quotes, fees are deductible business expense. Verify current fee schedule for his country.
- Turn 27 (2024-03-15): Darryl wants $150 dining budget; Alexis wanted $250; compromise $200 starting April. Asked how to make Excel work. Plan: shared dining budget $200/mo (~$46/wk), Excel with budget vs actual, SUMIFS, weekly tally, conditional formatting; note $150 can be personal stretch target only if agreed with Alexis; review at check-ins.
- Turn 28 (2024-03-15): Darryl asks to validate $200 dining compromise (starting April) and get tips to stick to it. Validated: 33% cut, shared agreement matters more than exact number; tips: define what counts as dining, weekly pace check, meal planning, planned social meals, overage rule, 60-90 day review.
- Turn 29 (2024-03-15): Darryl says EF now covers "nearly two months" (earlier said 1 month, Turn 23). Answer: 2 months is a solid step toward 3-month year-end goal; with irregular freelance income, 3 is the minimum, 6 is better long term. Asked for essentials total to compute exact target.
- Turn 30 (2024-03-15): Darryl asks how to track progress toward a $5,850 goal in Excel. Unclear what the goal is (not previously discussed; could be the 3-month EF target or other). Gave generic Excel savings tracker setup (goal cell, contributions log, running total, % complete, projected finish). Asked him to confirm what $5,850 is for and current balance.
- Turn 31 (2024-03-15): PREFERENCE: Darryl wants detailed expense breakdowns whenever budgeting is discussed. Provided a sub-line-item draft budget (rent $1,200 actual; other figures placeholders marked as estimates; dining $200 agreed; EF ~$433/mo = $100/wk; mom support $200 line; solo take-home ~$4,300 scenario; household income/Alexis share not included).
- Turn 32 (2024-03-15): Darryl asks how to dip into EF for unexpected expense and track it. Advice: define qualifying emergencies, withdrawal log tab in Excel (date, amount, reason, balance after, replenish-by date), formulas for net balance and replenishment, replenish first from next windfall/transfers, keep tax set-aside separate.
- Turn 33 (2024-03-15): Darryl says he's never used Excel for expenses. CONFLICT: Turn 14/earlier he said he's been tracking daily expenses in Excel since March 1. Flagged gently. Gave beginner walkthrough: tabs (Transactions, Budget, Savings, EF Withdrawals), columns, data validation dropdown, Table format, SUMIFS, CSV import, weekly routine.
- Session 2 (2024-06-10): Darryl (stressed) says Alexis suggested a joint savings account at First National Bank on May 5 to improve transparency on spending. Asked how to get both on the same page. Advised: joint account for shared bills/savings/dining budget, keep personal allowances, shared view of account (bank login/alerts, CSV export into the existing Excel), monthly money date, discussion threshold, agreed categories. Note: EF $2,000 goal date was June 30, 2024; check status. Bank feature details not verified.
- Session 2, turn 2 (2024-06-10): Darryl asks if Tamara's $500 investment-basics workshop (June 15, Montserrat Community Center) is worth it given the $2,000 EF goal by June 30. Advised: not worth prioritizing now; $500 would consume most of the remaining EF gap; check instructor credentials, fees/upsells, refund policy; cheaper free alternatives. Current EF balance not confirmed by user.
- Session 2, turn 3 (2024-06-10): Darryl chose free/low-cost investing education over the $500 workshop; says he's "a bit short" of $2,000 by June 30 (no balance given). Suggested: get exact balance, compute gap / remaining weeks, free resources (Investor.gov, Khan Academy, library ebooks, Bogle's Little Book of Common Sense Investing), no-spend days.
- Session 2, turn 4 (2024-06-10): Darryl frustrated with 3 months of daily expense tracking (felt like quitting May 30). Mom Ashlee's medical costs now $350/mo (up from $200 line). Advice: switch from daily manual entry to weekly bank CSV import plus manual cash only; track by category; keep Ashlee as fixed budget line; find the extra $150 from cuts, not emergency fund or tax set-aside.
- Session 2, turn 5-6 (2024-06-10): Cable cut $80 -> streaming $15 (June 1); saves $65/mo ($780/yr). EF reached $1,200 on June 5 (60% of $2,000); gap $800 to June 30. Asked for motivation tips.
- Session 2, turn 7 (2024-06-10): Paid off $1,000 credit card balance May 25; says it avoided ~$50/mo interest (implies ~60% APR). Asked how to stay on top of debt. Open: source of the payoff money (EF or other) unknown; other debts unknown.
- Session 2, turn 8 (2024-06-10): Dining out $300 (March) -> $180 (May), down 40%. Shared agreed dining budget with Alexis is $200/mo; original personal target $150. Asked for plan to cut further. Advice: target $150 only if agreed with Alexis; weekly cap ~$35; meal planning, delivery rule, define dining, route coffee to small misc.

## Session 3 (2024-12-05): Ashlee $300 request due Dec 10 + car by Dec 31 2026 (keywords: Ashlee, car, Dec 2024, medical)
- User is worried about Ashlee's medical expenses: $300 request due Dec 10, 2024; says he already approved a budget for it. Did not say whether $300 is one-time or part of the $350/mo line (June figure).
- Car goal restated as $15,000 by Dec 31, 2026 (~25 months from Dec 5 2024; ~24 full months Jan 2025-Dec 2026 => ~$625/mo for $15k, or ~$600/mo if counted from Dec 2024).
- Year-end EF target (3 months, Dec 31 2024) is 26 days away; status unknown since June (last: $1,200 of $2,000 on June 5). Sequencing: finish EF, then redirect the ~$433/mo EF contribution to car (~$10,400 by Dec 2026 at $433/mo x 24 months; gap ~$4,600).
- Each $100/mo of Ashlee spend = $2,400 over 24 months (~16% of the car goal).
- Advice given: pay the $300 from the approved Ashlee line, not EF or car fund; verify the bill (itemized statement, insurance EOBs, assistance programs) since cost rose $200->$350 in 3 months; decide on a monthly cap for Ashlee with family.
- Open items to ask: current EF balance, whether $300 is one-time, current monthly Ashlee total, Alexis's income/share, current car fund balance (a 2024-09-02 session note mentions a car fund but no details are saved).

## Session 4 (2024-12-05): Alexis freelance business + joint budget + groceries (keywords: Alexis, freelance, grocery, joint budget)
- Alexis (graphic designer) starts freelance design business Jan 2025, expects ~$2,000/mo initially (gross, unverified, irregular).
- Grocery budget raised to $500/mo from Sept 1 2024, then to $550/mo (prior grocery baseline not saved; % change unknown).
- Advice given: treat her income as variable; don't put full $2,000 in base budget; set aside tax (assumed ~25%, verify local rules) and business costs (PayPal ~3%, software); pay a fixed monthly draw to joint account, keep the rest in a separate business account; upside to car fund/EF; check food total (groceries $550 + dining $200) since dining cut ($300->$180) shifted spend to groceries.
- Open items: prior grocery baseline, whether grocery increase is funded by baseline income or her expected income, her actual Jan 2025 invoices, local tax rules for freelancers.

## Session 5 (2024-12-05): holiday gifts anxiety, $400 cap (keywords: holiday, gifts, $400, anxious)
- Darryl anxious about holiday spending; gifts budget capped at $400 total. Worried about going over.
- Advice given: split $400 into per-person allocations plus ~10% buffer; confirm whether food/travel/decor are inside or outside the gifts line; log each purchase when made; 80% ($320) switch-to-planned rule; overage rule = cut a planned gift or use a named flex line, never EF/car fund/Ashlee line; agree with Alexis since joint; anxiety tips (scheduled money check, no shopping while stressed).
- Open: recipient list, amounts already spent, whether holiday meals are in the gifts line.

## Session 6 (2024-12-05): documentary pitch invite, $12,000, due Dec 20 (keywords: Dwayne, documentary, pitch, $12,000)
- Darryl invited by colleague Dwayne (met at Montserrat Film Festival 2019) to pitch a $12,000 documentary project by Dec 20. Unsure whether to take it. Dwayne not previously mentioned; not verified.
- Advice: clarify whether $12k is a fee for him, a budget he would manage, or an investment being raised; whether pitch is paid or unpaid; any upfront payments requested (red flag); get written terms; tax set-aside on the fee; compare against car fund/EF; check deadline pressure.
- Open: terms, whether the pitch is paid, who funds it, his current freelance pipeline.
- Session 6 follow-up (2024-12-05): Darryl will talk to Alexis about the Dwayne pitch before deciding. Alexis's input covers his time/energy load and effect on financial goals (car fund, EF, joint budget, her Jan 2025 freelance income).

## Session 7 (2024-12-05): reduce production hours to 30/wk from Jan 2025 (keywords: hours, 30/week, reduce, income impact)
- Darryl considering cutting production hours to 30/wk from Jan 2025 to support Alexis's business launch.
- Rough estimate (assumes pay scales with hours, 40h baseline unverified): 25% cut on $65k gross (Mar 2024 figure) = ~$16k gross/yr, ~$1,000/mo net (~23% of $4,300 take-home est.).
- Fixed lines from our notes: rent $1,200 + Ashlee $350 + groceries $550 + dining $200 + EF $433 + car $600 = ~$3,333/mo, before utilities/other bills. Post-cut take-home ~$3,300: fixed lines alone roughly consume it. Alexis's income not counted in baseline until proven.
- Advice: confirm pay structure (salary vs per project); stagger start or make it conditional (EF at 3 months essentials, Alexis's 3-month avg net, car fund progress); check health insurance/retirement tied to hours; keep Dwayne pitch in mind as possible offset.

## Session 8 (2024-12-05): grocery $550 from Dec 1 for holiday meals/guests (keywords: groceries, holiday, $550, December)
- Darryl says grocery budget raised to $550/mo starting Dec 1 for holiday meals and guests. Earlier (Alexis session) notes said $500 from Sept 1, then $550 "later". Dates conflict; treat as possibly a December holiday bump, not necessarily permanent. Confirm.
- Advice: +$50 vs $500 base (+10%); offset December dining ($200 -> $150, needs Alexis agreement); revert to baseline in January unless intentionally permanent; track holiday food separately from the $400 gifts line; keep off EF/car fund/Ashlee line.
- Open: confirm whether $550 is temporary or permanent; guest count and menu; whether Alexis agreed to the dining offset.
